question: Which process is used by the unicellular freshwater organisms and most plant cells to take in water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Osmosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unicellular freshwater organisms and most plant cells tend to gain water through osmosis**.
 
• The absorption of water by plant roots is also an example of osmosis.
 
• Osmosis can be defined as **the spontaneous movement of solvent molecules through a semi-permeable membrane, from a low-concentration solution to a high-concentration solution.**
 
• Osmosis is purely a mechanical process where cells absorb water without spending any amount of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morphogenesis**

 
 
• ​**A biological process that causes a tissue or organ to develop its shape by controlling the spatial distribution of cells during embryonic development.**
 
 
 
• **Hybridisation**
 
 
• **​A process of mathematically combining two or more atomic orbitals from the same atom to form a completely different orbital from its constituents** is therefore called a hybrid orbital.
 
 
 
• **Tropism**
 
 
• **​The growth rate of plant parts in which the direction of stimulus determines the direction of response is called tropism.**
 
• Example: **Phototropism, where plant stems grow upward in response to sunlight.**
 
 

b1:T
